summary: This note is a clipped Wikipedia-style history of the Carolina Hurricanes, an NHL ice hockey team based in Raleigh, North Carolina. It traces the franchise from its founding as the New England Whalers in the WHA in 1971, through the move to Hartford and then to North Carolina in 1997, to its 2006 Stanley Cup title and later playoff droughts, ownership changes and coaching turnover up to 2021. The note ends mid-sentence while describing the 2020–21 season.
one_line: History of the Carolina Hurricanes NHL hockey franchise, from its 1971 New England Whalers origins through its 2006 Stanley Cup win and later years.
key_facts: The Carolina Hurricanes are a professional ice hockey team based in Raleigh, North Carolina, and play home games at PNC Arena.
The franchise was formed in 1971 as the New England Whalers of the World Hockey Association (WHA).
The Whalers joined the NHL in 1979 as part of the NHL–WHA merger and were renamed the Hartford Whalers.
The team relocated to North Carolina in 1997 and rebranded as the Hurricanes; owner Peter Karmanos chose the name himself.
The Hurricanes played home games in Greensboro for their first two seasons after the move, and the note says most games there attracted crowds of 5,000 or fewer.
The Hurricanes first advanced to the Stanley Cup Finals in 2002, where they lost to the Detroit Red Wings.
The Hurricanes won the 2006 Stanley Cup over the Edmonton Oilers, winning Game 7 by a score of 3–1.
Cam Ward was awarded the Conn Smythe Trophy as the 2006 playoffs' most valuable player, becoming just the fourth rookie to receive it.
In 2009, the Hurricanes beat the New Jersey Devils in Game 7 of the first round in what the note calls the 'Shock at the Rock'.
Jeff Skinner won the Calder Memorial Trophy as rookie of the year in the 2010–11 season, the first Hurricanes player to receive that honor.
Tom Dundon was announced as the buyer of the Hurricanes on December 7, 2017, and the deal was finalized on January 11, 2018, ensuring the team would not be relocated.
Rod Brind'Amour was named head coach in 2018 and won the Jack Adams Award as the NHL's best coach in 2021.
The Hurricanes clinched a playoff spot on April 4, 2019, and reached the Eastern Conference Finals that year before being swept by the Boston Bruins.
On February 22, 2020, emergency goaltender David Ayres became the first emergency goaltender in NHL history to win a game, a 6–3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs.
The 2020–21 season ended with the Hurricanes winning the Central Division, their first division title since winning the Southeast Division in 2006.
